visual_blocks.heading: ASCII MASTER FLOW - PANEL 2/12: Three dates that must not be merged
visual_blocks.preview: JULY 1905 -> partition announced

visual_blocks.heading: ASCII MASTER FLOW - PANEL 3/12: Administrative pretext versus political reading
visual_blocks.preview: OFFICIAL CASE -> Bengal was too large for efficient administration

visual_blocks.heading: ASCII MASTER FLOW - PANEL 4/12: Swadeshi and boycott were complementary
visual_blocks.preview: BOYCOTT / NEGATIVE ARM -> refuse foreign goods and selected institutions

visual_blocks.heading: ASCII MASTER FLOW - PANEL 5/12: The constructive programme built institutions
visual_blocks.preview: INDUSTRY -> indigenous production, stores and investment

visual_blocks.heading: ASCII MASTER FLOW - PANEL 6/12: Cultural mobilisation widened and narrowed politics
visual_blocks.preview: WIDENED -> songs, festivals, processions and Vande Mataram

visual_blocks.heading: ASCII MASTER FLOW - PANEL 7/12: Militant nationalism was a programme, not a mood
visual_blocks.preview: SWARAJ -> political objective and moral self-rule

visual_blocks.heading: ASCII MASTER FLOW - PANEL 8/12: Regional spread was uneven
visual_blocks.preview: BENGAL -> anti-partition core, samitis, education and cultural action

visual_blocks.heading: ASCII MASTER FLOW - PANEL 9/12: Participation expanded but did not become fully mass
visual_blocks.preview: VISIBLE CORE -> students, professionals and urban middle classes

visual_blocks.heading: ASCII MASTER FLOW - PANEL 10/12: Congress compromise gave way to the Surat rupture
visual_blocks.preview: BANARAS 1905 -> Congress accepted Swadeshi and Bengal boycott

visual_blocks.heading: ASCII MASTER FLOW - PANEL 11/12: Decline and legacy moved in opposite directions
visual_blocks.preview: DECLINE -> repression, arrests, deportation and press controls
